factor_name: Organization capital to book assets, ranked within industry; OMK high-minus-low factor
paper_ref: Eisfeldt and Papanikolaou, Journal of Finance, August 2013, 68(4), 1365-1406
economic_intuition: Organization capital is embodied in key talent; shareholders do not own all cash-flow rights, so high organization-capital firms expose shareholders to additional risk and command higher returns.
detailed_definition: Stock of organization capital constructed by cumulating deflated SG&A expenses using the perpetual inventory method, scaled by book assets and ranked relative to industry peers.

source_details: common shares traded on NYSE, AMEX, or NASDAQ
cpit denotes the consumer price index

required_fields.concept: Selling, general, and administrative expenses used as flows to organization capital.
required_fields.source_detail: The paper constructs organization capital using SG&A expenditures.

required_fields.concept: Consumer price index used to deflate SG&A expenses.
required_fields.source_detail: Equation (35) divides SG&A by cpit, denoted as the consumer price index.

required_fields.concept: Book assets K used to scale organization capital; Table III notes Compustat item at.
required_fields.source_detail: The paper scales O by book assets and Table III notes Compustat item at.

required_fields.concept: 17-industry grouping used to compute within-industry O/K quintile ranks.
required_fields.source_detail: The paper groups firms into 17 industries based on Fama and French (1997).

required_fields.source_detail: The sample includes Compustat firms with fiscal year ending in December.

required_fields.concept: Nonfinancial firm indicator or SIC-derived financial firm exclusion.

formula.expression: organization_capital_t / book_assets_t, where organization_capital_t is recursively accumulated from SGA_t / CPI_t with constants delta_o=0.15 and g=0.10

evidence.interpretation: Section II.A states the recursive perpetual-inventory method, the 15% depreciation rate, the 10% SG&A growth parameter, missing-SG&A treatment, scaling by book assets, and within-industry O/K ranking.

evidence.quote: rebalance these portfolios in June every year
evidence.interpretation: This directly supports annual June rebalancing.

evidence.quote: missing values in the SG&A as zero
evidence.interpretation: The paper gives a specific missing policy for SG&A and states sample filters for other fields.

portfolio.universe: Nonfinancial Compustat firms with fiscal year ending in December and common shares traded on NYSE, AMEX, or NASDAQ, with nonmissing SIC codes and nonzero organization capital.

evidence.interpretation: The paper ranks firms into O/K quintiles within each of 17 industries.
